triggers: Found nearly all year; frost-resistant, can be dug out under snow in winter (de.wikipedia). Most common in autumn (en.wikipedia); first-nature also says mainly winter/spring. No rain or temperature numbers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Elevation 100-1000 m unverified (no source gives altitude). Sources call it a weak parasite on living wood as well as saprotroph. Conifers (Picea) only very rarely. Sources disagree on peak (autumn vs winter/spring).

triggers: Native Central European strains need temps below 11 C to fruit and tolerate frost down to -2.8 C (Bresinsky, via de.wikipedia). Historically a winter mushroom; also summer to early winter in first-nature.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Populus and Salix not named in fetched sources (beech, oaks, 'other hardwoods'); rarely conifers. Catalogue months include Jan-Apr; sources describe autumn-early winter (winter strain), so Jan-Mar possible but not quantified. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers in sources. Prefers moderately dry, base- and nutrient-poor soils; on limestone only superficially acidified soil (de.wikipedia). Often in young plantations and sparse moss/grass spots.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources give Jun-Nov (de) / Jun-Oct to Nov (first-nature), catalogue Jun-Oct. Preferred partner in Central Europe is Picea, then Fagus; Pinus missing from catalogue. Elevation unverified. Abundance from Germany, no RO source.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers. Avoids waterlogged, rapidly drying, alkaline and nutrient-rich soils; sandy to slightly loamy, acid to neutral soils (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue starts in June; de.wikipedia gives Jul-Oct for Central Europe (Jun mentioned for the genus in general). 'Conifers' = Picea in sources; Carpinus added. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers. In Central Europe mainly in higher parts of the low mountain ranges, very rare at low elevation (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Soil: de.wikipedia says acid soils preferred; first-nature and en.wikipedia say alkaline/neutral/chalky - sources disagree. Season Jul-Dec in sources vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Abies not named as partner; Quercus added. Higher-elevation tendency supported, numbers not.

triggers: Prefers warm sites for fruiting (de.wikipedia). Emerges from wounds and cavities of living or dead standing hardwoods, sometimes several metres up. No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Jun-Sep; sources Jun-Oct (de) and Jul-Nov (first-nature). Substrate sources differ: living/dead standing trees (de, en) vs dead trunks (first-nature). Rare in Germany; elevation unverified.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers stated. Mainly in conifer forests, less often broadleaf.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue omits Picea, which de.wikipedia names first (Fichten, Birken); Pinus/Betula supported by first-nature. Association with Amanita muscaria not stated in sources. Catalogue starts Jun; source says Jul-Oct. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Typically nutrient-rich soils in forests and parks, few special requirements (de.wikipedia); also reported in grasslands and hardwood/conifer woods (en.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Neither source states a mycorrhizal host; trophic mode 'm' and host list are not confirmed. Season Jul-Nov vs catalogue Jun-Oct. Elevation unverified. Abundance from Germany.

triggers: No numbers. Moist, loamy, calcareous soils in mixed deciduous forest (de.wikipedia); first-nature notes woodland edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources Aug-Nov (de) vs catalogue Sep-Nov. Oak also named as partner. en.wikipedia (mostly North American) says mostly coniferous woods, which disagrees with de/first-nature (beech). Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Appears mostly in autumn and late autumn (de.wikipedia); clusters at base of living or dead trunks.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Matches catalogue months. Sources say saprobic or weakly parasitic on living or dead wood, also conifers (Picea) occasionally; apple (Malus) at trunk base named by de.wikipedia. Elevation unverified. Abundance from Germany ('very common').

triggers: Thermophilic: warm, south-facing limestone sites (tintling). Main season July-August (pilzbuch-pilzwelten); late Jul to mid Sep, rarely early Oct (tintling). No rain numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Matches catalogue months roughly (sources Jun-Aug to early Oct). Beech is the main partner in German sources; oak per en.wikipedia (southern Europe). Rare in most Central European limestone areas. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Mostly beech, beech-fir, oak-hornbeam and spruce-fir forests; avoids pure spruce stands (de.wikipedia). Less common in lowlands, more in low mountain ranges (en.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Picea (secondary) and Quercus named by sources; Abies only 'rarely'. Months consistent (Jul-Oct to Jul-Nov). Low-mountain tendency supported, numeric 400-1200 m not.

triggers: No numbers. Strictly bound to larch; mainly on lime-rich soils (de.wikipedia); calcareous or sandy soils (first-nature). Alpine-subalpine and montane areas.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent with catalogue (Larix, Jul-Oct). Adds lime-rich soil preference. Described as uncommon to rare in en.wikipedia, not very dense in de. Elevation 500-1600 m unverified.

triggers: Rainy weather can bring fruitbodies as early as July (de.wikipedia). Acid, base- and nutrient-poor, moderately to clearly moist soils, among mosses; often fruits in large numbers. No rain numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Months consistent (Aug-Nov, July after rain). Deciduous partners (beech) occasional. en.wikipedia describes North American hosts and Nov-Jan season, not applicable to Europe. Elevation 600-1700 m unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Also on grassy forest edges and unkept lawns (de/en.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: No source names specific host genera (only 'both conifer and broadleaf forests'), so hosts left empty. Months match (Jun-Oct de; Jul-Oct first-nature). Elevation unverified. Abundance 'common, widely distributed' (de, en), 'infrequent' in Britain.

triggers: No numbers. Saprotroph in woods, especially in needle litter under spruce (de.wikipedia); in all kinds of woodland (first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Oct (Jul-Nov) vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Litter is mostly conifer (spruce) per de.wikipedia; first-nature says all woodland. Elevation unverified. Spelled silvicola in de/en wikipedia.

triggers: No numbers. Acidified, sandy, well-drained soils, forest tracks, shaded banks and drainage-ditch sides (de.wikipedia, first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: No source names host genera (Quercus, Betula, Pinus unconfirmed); de.wikipedia stresses dry sandy conifer and mixed forests. Season Jul-Nov vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Prefers acid sandy, loamy or silicate soils but tolerates limestone (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources name many more partners (Abies, Betula, Carpinus, Quercus) than catalogue (Fagus, Picea). Season Jun-Oct (de), Jul-Nov (first-nature); Jul-Oct kept. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Acid, fresh soils; rare or absent in calcareous areas; warm oak and oak-hornbeam forests, also beech forests (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent with catalogue (Quercus, Jul-Oct). Castanea only in southern Europe. Never fruits in large numbers in Germany (scattered to rare), common in UK. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says broadleaf and conifer. de.wikipedia: deciduous partners; conifer records may be related species; first-nature still says broadleaf and conifer. Disagreement. Months Aug-Nov vs Jun-Oct UK; catalogue kept. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Fruits April to late October and in mild winter spells (en.wikipedia); all year, most plentiful in summer-autumn (first-nature). Often when few other fungi are out.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue includes Nov; sources say Apr-Oct plus mild winters. Birch/beech/alder named; rarely conifers. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Lying trunks, stumps and dead roots of spruce; benefits from forestry planting of spruce and pine (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent (Jul-Nov, conifer wood). Very rarely on broadleaf wood. Elevation 500-1600 m unverified; very common in German planted spruce stands at all levels.

triggers: No numbers. Lean meadows and pastures in hill country, also forest clearings (de.wikipedia); closely mown unfertilised grassland, upland acid pastures (first-nature). Intolerant of heavy fertiliser.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Sep-Nov (de) vs Aug-Dec (first-nature); catalogue Aug-Nov. Montane tendency ('im Bergland') but no altitude numbers; catalogue 300-2000 m unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Autumn species; earliest at higher altitudes (first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Picea not confirmed (sources say only 'occasionally conifers'). Soil: en.wikipedia acidic vs first-nature alkaline/chalk - disagree. Not common anywhere in Europe. Season Jul-Nov (first-nature) broader than catalogue. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Groups and fairy rings in broadleaf woodland and woodland edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No source names Fagus or a mycorrhizal host; trophic mode unconfirmed. Season Jul-Oct (pilzfinder, var. nidorosum) / summer to late autumn (first-nature) vs catalogue Aug-Oct. Abundance 'very common' only from UK source. Elevation unverified.

triggers: Early spring after snowmelt, around leaf-out, before true morels (en.wikipedia). Does not fruit every year; warm sites, often in floodplains (de.wikipedia). Cited 3-30 C range is mycelial growth, not fruiting.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Fraxinus not named in sources (poplar, willow, aspen near riverbanks). Catalogue includes March; de.wikipedia gives Apr-May. Locally common on calcareous floodplain soils, otherwise rare. Elevation unverified.

triggers: July-August rain essential for fruiting (trufamania); tolerates summer rain up to 180% of normal, drought reduces mycelium; fruitbodies need at least 0.4 C during winter formation (en.wikipedia). Soil pH ~7.7.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No fetched source records it in Romania (Italy, Istria, Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia etc.); Romanian occurrence unconfirmed. Season Sep-early Jan (de) / late Sep-late Nov. Oak is most frequent host; poplar secondary. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Warm beech forests on base-rich, nutrient-poor soils (lime, marl); some forms fruit at snowbank edges in spring in North America (en.wikipedia, not Europe).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent (Fagus, Quercus, Jul-Oct; de Aug-Oct, first-nature Jul-Nov). Pine only in warmer regions. Rare and declining in Germany (RL 2). Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Warm summer months, occasionally to October (de.wikipedia). Basic, dry to fresh soils; sedge-beech and oak-hornbeam forests.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Carpinus not named as partner (only as forest type); beech and oak lead. Season Jul-Oct vs catalogue Jun-Sep. Lower altitudes supported (en.wikipedia), 100-800 m not numerically confirmed. Red List 3 in Germany, endangered in Czechia.

triggers: No numbers. Main season end of August to end of October (de.wikipedia). Grows on acid, neutral and alkaline soils; abundant even on thin soil and steep run-off slopes (first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Jul-Nov vs catalogue Aug-Nov. Lowland, hill and lower montane, rarely higher (de.wikipedia), consistent with 100-900 m but no numbers.

triggers: No rain/frost numbers. Lean, nutrient-poor grazed grassland; avoids forest and calcareous areas (de.wikipedia). Mild sites occasionally to January. Observed in quantity at 1400-1700 m (Tirol) and 820-1300 m (Black Forest).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Oct (to Jan locally) vs catalogue Aug-Nov. Lowland to alpine in sources; 400-2000 m not stated as a range. en.wikipedia says rich acidic soil; de says nutrient-poor.

triggers: No numbers. Examined collections from September and October (czechmycology). Moist places along creeks, paths and roadsides, with Urtica or Rubus; well-decayed wood, twigs, acorns, cones.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: mostly broadleaved or mixed forest, less often conifer (catalogue stresses mixed and conifer). Not specifically buried wood. Season rests on Sep-Oct records only. 'Common in Central Europe' (en.wikipedia) vs 'very poorly known' (czechmycology). Probably submontane-montane.
